title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Google’s Gemini app surpasses 750 million monthly active users, intensifying competition in the AI market and fueling speculation about a potential Apple partnership. Andreessen Horowitz invested $1.7 billion in AI infrastructure, including OpenAI and ElevenLabs, further demonstrating confidence in the sector. ElevenLabs’ valuation soared to $11 billion following a $500 million funding round, highlighting the rapid growth in specialized AI. Sam Altman publicly criticized Claude’s Super Bowl ads, reflecting the high stakes in AI market leadership.

KKR and Singtel acquired STT GDC for $5.2 billion, reflecting the growing demand for digital infrastructure. Advanced Micro Devices is betting on its MI450 AI accelerator for future growth. General Motors increased its dividend, signaling financial strength.

Globally, the expiration of the New Start treaty raises concerns about a potential nuclear arms race. The US is implementing a plan to counter China’s dominance in critical minerals. Tensions between the US and China escalated with Xi Jinping’s warning to Trump regarding Taiwan. In Nigeria, escalating violence prompted a US military deployment.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street opened defensively on Thursday, February 5, 2026, with the S&P 500 down 0.51% and the Nasdaq 100 declining 1.77%. The session was characterized by a strengthening US Dollar, broader risk aversion, and declining commodity prices, including crude oil and gold. The 10-Year Treasury Yield decreased to 4.258%, while the US Dollar Index rose to 97.63.

Overnight, Asian markets exhibited mixed performance; Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.88%, while Greater China saw the Hang Seng rise 0.14% and the Shanghai Composite decline 0.64%. European markets followed a cautious trend, influenced by mixed economic data including a rise in German industrial orders and an easing slump in UK construction.

US futures reflected this cautious sentiment, with S&P 500 futures down 0.67% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.02%. Investors are anticipating central bank decisions from the ECB and Bank of England, alongside the Challenger survey’s planned layoffs data and European economic indicators. The market’s path appears to be downward, awaiting developments from these key catalysts.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap by AGI Era on February 5, 2026, reported a negative day for US markets. The S&P 500 fell 1.23%, closing at 6798.4, while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.38% to 24548.69 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 592.58 points to 48908.72. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a lack of strong conviction.

A notable sector rotation occurred, with investors moving into defensive Utilities (XLU.US) which gained 0.09%, while Technology (XLK.US) fell 1.82%, indicating a shift towards safety amid weaker-than-expected labor market readings. The 10-Year Treasury Yield eased to 4.26%, reflecting tempered inflation expectations. The US Dollar Index rose 0.35% to 97.83, and Crude Oil (CL.F) decreased 3.16% to $63.08.

Tech giants experienced significant declines, with Microsoft down 4.97%, Amazon down 4.42%, and Nvidia down 1.27%. This downturn highlighted a broader re-evaluation of growth stocks due to concerns about the economic slowdown. The VIX, the “Fear Gauge,” remained subdued despite the sell-off. Applied Materials (AMAT) saw a notable increase in after-hours trading.

Looking ahead, the market awaits no major economic data releases but will closely monitor Federal Reserve commentary and further labor market updates. The overall tone remains cautious, with investors seeking signs of stabilization or deterioration in economic indicators.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary: Russia and Ukraine executed a prisoner exchange, the first since October, returning 157 Ukrainian and 160 Russian servicemen. Peace talks concluded without a breakthrough, highlighting the ongoing humanitarian dimensions of the conflict despite stalled diplomatic efforts. In Lebanon, Israel was accused of spraying villages with herbicide, raising concerns about potential environmental and agricultural consequences. A massacre in Nigeria killed at least 78 Muslims, fueling insurgent activity and demanding a stronger regional response. U.S. and Iranian nuclear talks began in Oman, aiming to de-escalate tensions regarding Iran’s nuclear program. In South Sudan, aid workers went missing after airstrikes hit a hospital, raising concerns about humanitarian protection. Fifty-five thousand Ukrainian soldiers were killed, and tens of thousands remain missing, significantly increasing the human cost of the war. Finally, an Israeli intelligence chief’s brother was charged with smuggling cigarettes into Gaza, highlighting potential vulnerabilities in conflict zones. These events underscore a protracted conflict with significant geopolitical implications, impacting economies and international alliances.
